name: IAEA

summary.text: The International Atomic Energy Agency is the Vienna-based UN-system body that verifies states' nuclear safeguards obligations. On June 12, 2025 its Board of Governors adopted a resolution drafted by France, Germany and the United Kingdom and backed by the United States finding Iran in non-compliance with its safeguards obligations, the first such finding in two decades; the vote was 19 in favour, three against (Russia, China and Burkina Faso), with 11 abstentions. The IAEA's preceding quarterly report put Iran's stockpile of uranium enriched to 60% at 408.6 kg.

openQuestions: The site's statement that the IAEA reported 408.6 kg of uranium at 60% and found Iran in non-compliance on 12 June is supported; the 408.6 kg figure comes from the quarterly report preceding the vote rather than the resolution text.
The IAEA Board document (GOV/2025 series) and the May 2025 safeguards report on iaea.org were not reachable and should be cited directly; vote counts for later resolutions differ across sources.
